title: Fix the temperature chart feed
prompt: The temperature chart needs every reading with a usable temperature. The function below throws away readings the chart could use and still lets the -9999 code through. Fix `solve(observations)`.
rules: A temperature is usable unless `temperature_c` is empty (null) or holds the station's `-9999` code.
Keep a reading even when other columns are empty, NaN or -9999: the chart plots only the temperature.
Return every column of `observations` with its values unchanged, duplicates included.
hints: Run the starter and compare: a reading with a faulty rain gauge is missing. `dropna()` with no arguments drops a row when any column is empty or NaN.
`dropna(subset=[...])` looks only at the columns you list.
-9999 isn't null, so `dropna` keeps it. Add a `filter` that leaves out that code, without changing any value.
explanation: `dropna()` with no arguments checks every column, and for decimal-point columns it treats NaN as missing too, so a reading with a good temperature but a faulty rain gauge, or no quality flag, disappears. Limiting it with `subset=["temperature_c"]` fixes that. The -9999 code is a real number, so `dropna` never sees it; a `filter` removes it: `observations.dropna(subset=["temperature_c"]).filter(F.col("temperature_c") != -9999)`. In fact the filter alone is enough, because `!= -9999` isn't true for an empty temperature either. Don't replace -9999 in every column first: that would change the humidity, wind and pressure values of readings the chart keeps.
